canonical_question: Do the reported cyan internal friction curves include baseline contributions, and is a correlation index of >0.99 sufficient to rule out alternative peak composition models in high-temperature regions?

question_variants.question: Does the cyan curve representing the sum of cumulative fitting peaks include the baseline internal friction, or is it solely the sum of the fitted Snoek components?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The cyan curves represent the sum of the cumulative fitting peaks only; the text does not explicitly state if a baseline internal friction is included in this sum.

answers.answer: The document states that the cyan curves are the sum of the cumulative fitting peaks, but does not specify inclusion of a baseline.
answers.measurement_outcome: Cyan curves represent sum of cumulative fitting peaks
evidence_spans: For the nitrogen-doped N-2 HEA, an additional low-temperature peak (blue curve) and two high-temperature peaks (green and magenta curves) were also observed (see Fig. 5C ).
The peak height of the additional low-temperature peak is 0.002, and that of the two high-temperature peaks is 0.027 and 0.009, respectively.
Hence, only ~5.3% of all the nitrogen atoms in the N-2 HEA contribute to the formation of ordered nitrogen complexes.

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: The available answers confirm that cyan curves represent the sum of cumulative fitting peaks and that the correlation index for these fits exceeds 0.99.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The analysis focuses on clarifying the definition of the plotted data (component composition) versus validating the statistical adequacy of the fit model. One approach defines the data construction, while the other evaluates the statistical threshold for model exclusion.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: These findings are specific to the nitrogen-doped (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi) 98 N 2 alloy measured under variable temperature conditions.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: There are no direct contradictions between the provided answers. However, both answers explicitly note the absence of information regarding specific assumptions (baseline inclusion) and limitations (sufficiency of the R-squared value to exclude alternatives).
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: The evidence is observational regarding the existence of the cyan curves and the numerical value of the correlation index. It is limited by the explicit lack of discussion on baseline inclusion and the exclusion power of the statistical metric in the source text.
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: It remains unknown whether the cyan curves incorporate a baseline internal friction component or if the >0.99 correlation index is sufficient to definitively rule out alternative models with different peak compositions in the high-temperature region.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The cyan curves likely represent only the sum of the fitted Snoek components without an explicit baseline term, and the >0.99 correlation, while indicating a good fit, does not statistically rule out alternative models due to potential overfitting or non-unique solutions in the high-temperature region.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: A study should explicitly plot the baseline component separately or add it to the sum of peaks to visualize the difference, and employ a model selection criterion (e.g., AIC or BIC) alongside the correlation index to statistically compare the current model against alternative peak compositions.
